title: Debate of the Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: Ye Qing's deep, dark eyes stared straight at him, her voice low and bewitching: "If... there was a person who could let you escape this chessboard, would you dare to gamble?"

text.content: The night was as black as ink, the cold wind carried the dampness of the mountains. Chen Ji sat alone at the cliff's edge, his knuckles white from gripping the jade slip. The words on the slip were branded into his mind like a searing iron—"The Chen bloodline, generation after generation, all are chess pieces." Was all his struggle and scheming over these years never beyond the chessboard? Rage burned in his chest like wildfire, shaking every organ within him.

dialogue.content: "Sitting here alone—are you planning to jump, or waiting for someone?" Ye Qing's voice drifted from the darkness, carrying a hint of mockery. She walked over gracefully, the aura of a Holy Sect's saint flickering in the night air. "The Tianji Record's energy fluctuations are intense. What happened?"

text.content: Chen Ji raised his head, the fire of rage still unextinguished, but he forced it down, leaving only an abyss of cold intent. He handed the jade slip to Ye Qing, his voice terrifyingly calm: "Look at this." Ye Qing took the jade slip, and the moment her spiritual sense entered it, her pupils contracted sharply—the line of text, she saw it clearly.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji decided to show Ye Qing more truths from the Tianji Record, but he needed to decide how much to reveal.

choices.description: Let Ye Qing see all records about the Chen family's fate in the Tianji Record, including the deliberately concealed truths.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Ye Qing's deeper understanding and possible assistance
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing might know too much and become an unstable factor

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and retrieved the Tianji Record Fragment. A vision of light and shadow unfolded slowly between the two of them. It showed the images of the Chen ancestors through the ages—they struggled, resisted, submitted, and ultimately all fell at the same destination. Ye Qing's breathing quickened.

choices.description: Only let Ye Qing see the part about "chess pieces," keeping other key information as a trump card.
choices.visible_cost: Ye Qing might feel there are reservations
choices.visible_reward: Maintain information superiority, not fully revealing trump cards
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing might develop doubts because of this
choices.process_label: 有选择地展示部分真相

text.content: Chen Ji narrowed his eyes slightly, only transmitting that passage from the jade slip to Ye Qing via spiritual sense. The vision flashed by, and he stopped in time, only showing her the tip of the iceberg. Ye Qing frowned slightly, seemingly dissatisfied.

dialogue.content: After Ye Qing finished reading, she was silent for a long while. When she spoke again, her voice carried a gravity Chen Ji had never heard before: "Chen bloodline, generation after generation as chess pieces... Do you understand what this means?" She raised her head, those deep dark eyes flickering with complex light: "It means the hand that controls you is far larger than you imagined."

Chen Ji coldly laughed, the smile full of self-mockery: "I thought I was the chess player, so it turns out I was just being self-righteous on someone else's chessboard." His hand slowly clenched tight, nails digging deep into his palm, blood seeping through his fingers: "Ridiculous, utterly ridiculous!"

"Ridiculous?" Ye Qing suddenly laughed lightly, that smile carrying an inexplicable flavor: "Chen Ji, do you know who the Demonic Path commander is?" She paused, her voice extremely low: "He is also one of the 'Twin Births'—like you, a chess piece chosen by fate."

choice.prompt: The Demonic Path commander is also a chess piece of fate? This information was too shocking, and Chen Ji needed to decide how to respond.

choices.text: Inquire About the Twin Births Details
choices.description: Deeply question Ye Qing about the information on "Twin Births," trying to piece together more truth.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more clues about the fate chess game

text.content: Light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes: "Twin Births? How much do you know?" Sensing the urgency in his words, Ye Qing's lips slightly curled upward: "Why the rush? This secret... I can use it to exchange for a promise from you."

choices.description: Suppress the inner turmoil and probe what Ye Qing knows from a bystander's stance.
choices.visible_cost: Might miss the opportunity to learn more deeply
choices.visible_reward: Maintain negotiation initiative, not exposing trump cards
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing might no longer reveal more

text.content: Chen Ji suppressed his anger, his expression反而平静下来. He looked at Ye Qing with a half-smile: "You know quite a lot. But... why would a Holy Sect's saint tell me this?" Those eyes seemed to say: I know you have an agenda.

Ye Qing laughed lightly, that smile carrying a hint of bitterness: "Because we're all chess pieces." She extended her hand, and in the moonlight that hand was fair as jade, yet faint blue veins were visible: "You think the Holy Sect controls me only with poison? No, it's with 'fate'—my life, long ago, stopped being my own."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent. Ye Qing's words were like a sharp blade, cutting open the truth he had been evading. He slowly stood up, gazing toward the distant Tianqing Sect, his voice hoarse: "I once thought, as long as I was clever enough, patient enough, I could break out of this chess game." He bitterly smiled: "It turns out, from the very beginning, there was no distinction between inside and outside the chessboard."

text.content: "But there's one thing you haven't figured out." Ye Qing walked closer to him, her voice low: "Since we're all chess pieces, then why is it that you of all people obtained the Tianji Record? Why is it that I can understand that prophecy?" Her eyes gleamed with异样光芒 in the moonlight: "This itself... isn't it a kind of possibility?"

choice.prompt: Ye Qing's words gave Chen Ji a glimpse of the possibility of breaking the game, but this possibility was full of unknowns.

choices.description: Since fate gave them the special identity of chess pieces, perhaps it was precisely for them to break the chess game.
choices.visible_cost: Might be fooled by fate again
choices.visible_reward: Gain the theoretical possibility of breaking the game

dialogue.content: Chen Ji turned around, staring directly into Ye Qing's eyes: "You mean... we chess pieces might have been variables the chessboard planted for itself?" His voice carried a tremor, whether from excitement or fear: "If that's really the case, then let me see—just what game does this chessboard want to play!"

choices.description: This idea is too optimistic; one cannot easily believe in so-called "possibilities."
choices.visible_cost: Might miss a real opportunity to break the game
choices.visible_reward: Stay rational, not be misled by false hope
choices.process_label: 质疑这个可能的真实性

text.content: Chen Ji did not respond immediately but fell into deep contemplation. After a moment, he shook his head: "This is too much like a trap. If fate truly has a will, why would it give chess pieces the possibility to break free?" His tone was ice-cold: "Unless... this is exactly what it wants."

Upon hearing this, Ye Qing did not get angry but laughed instead. That laughter was exceptionally clear in the silent night, yet also carried a trace of desolation: "You're right, Chen Ji." Her gaze deepened: "But have you considered—if even doubt is designed, then whether you doubt or not, what's the difference?"

dialogue.content: "So..." Ye Qing's voice suddenly dropped, carrying a seriousness never seen before: "Rather than passively waiting for death, it's better to actively crash forward. Even if we crash until we're bloodied... at least—" She paused: "At least prove we're still alive."

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent. Looking at this Holy Sect's saint before him, he suddenly felt she was somewhat similar to himself—both were chess pieces caught in fate's grip, yet neither was willing to be a piece to be manipulated. The night wind blew past, fluttering both their robes. After a long while, Chen Ji spoke: "Tell me, what exactly do you want to do?"

dialogue.content: A flash of惊喜 appeared in Ye Qing's eyes, then quickly faded to calm. She took a deep breath and drew from her sleeve a pitch-black token, on which a twisted rune was carved: "This is the core of the Holy Sect's forbidden formation. If you can unravel it..." Her voice dropped extremely low: "You can sever fate's control over some of the chess pieces. And Mo Xiansheng in your Tianji Record might know the remaining keys."

text.content: Chen Ji stared at that token, his pupils slightly dilating. He understood the weight of this thing—Ye Qing was wagering her life. "Aren't you afraid I'll take the token and then betray you?" Chen Ji asked heavily. Ye Qing smiled, that smile carrying a sense of释然: "I am. But compared to continuing to be a chess piece... I want to see what scenery lies after the chessboard shatters."

Chen Ji reached out, and the moment his fingertip touched the token, a cold aura rushed along his meridians straight to his heart. He saw countless points of light—those were the threads of fate, connecting all living beings under heaven. And among those points of light, one thread was exceptionally brilliant, connecting in two directions: one was him, the other... was a blurry figure. That figure's outline strongly resembled his long-missing sister—Chen Nian.

"Chen Nian..." Chen Ji murmured, his voice trembling. That thread was so fragile, as if it might break at any moment, yet tenaciously connected the two ends of fate. Ye Qing sensed his strangeness, her brow furrowed: "What do you see?" Chen Ji did not answer, only tightly gripping the token, his knuckles white from the force.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's deep, dark eyes stared straight at him, her voice low and bewitching: "If... there was a person who could let you escape this chessboard, would you dare to gamble?" The night wind rose suddenly, dispersing the last trace of distance between them. In the distance, the lights of Tianqing Sect flickered dimly, and farther away, the horns of the Demonic Path army's advance could already be faintly heard. Chen Ji gripped the token tightly, his eyes flickering with complex light—rage, unwillingness, and also a spark of hope that had never been extinguished.
